## Current State

`verify.js --baseline` (#3043) classifies a failing test file as `baseline-flaky` when it fails in the full run but passes when re-run alone at HEAD, and prints one `CAVEAT: baseline-flaky:` line. The verdict goes nowhere else:
- It is never counted into the count stamp's `flakyHits`. That is the counter #1925's allowlisted retry feeds, and it drives the five-hit `flaky-allowlist` escalation caveat.
- It never stages a proposal to add the file to `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`'s `flaky.files`.

A file that keeps passing only in isolation is therefore invisible beyond each run's own CAVEAT.

Evidence: #3043's final whole-branch review follow-up I3 (ledger row 17). In the live runs, `tests/bin-lib/gif/palette.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/file-lock.test.js` each landed as baseline-flaky.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Count every `baselineAdjudicated.flakyPassed` file into `flakyHits` exactly as a retried allowlisted file is counted, in the count stamp's existing shape.
- [ ] A file whose hits reach the escalation threshold without being on `flaky.files` stages a `flaky-allowlist` proposal for the Review Console. It is never applied silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After two adjudicated runs in which the same file is baseline-flaky, the count stamp's `flakyHits` holds that file at 2.
- [ ] At the threshold, a staged allowlist proposal names the file and its hit count, and `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` is unchanged until the proposal is approved.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._

## Release Note

Flaky results from baseline verification now count toward the flaky-allowlist escalation threshold.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Claude Code 2.1.283+ ships a built-in `/prompt-audit` command. It reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, and flags instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules (source in the original request below).

What claude-tweaks already has in this space:

- `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md`) audits `.claude/skills/*.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md` and CLAUDE.md against the codebase, a template, and best practice, one target per firing. It then files `by:harness-health` issues. Its stated scope is the project's own `.claude/` tree (this repo has 17 files under `.claude/skills/`), not the 39 shipped `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` files. Its target discovery reads only `<root>/.claude/skills` (`plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/scope.js:198`).
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is a manual checklist to re-run whenever a new Claude model ships. It covers model-version deltas and a verification/self-check instruction audit against `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md`. That is the "instructions written for older models" concern, done by hand.

So the open question has two parts: what `/prompt-audit` catches that neither harness-health nor the manual model-version checklist catches, and whether it reaches the shipped `plugin/skills/` library at all.

## Deliverables

1. Run `/prompt-audit` once against this repo's CLAUDE.md, `.claude/skills/`, `plugin/skills/`, and `plugin/agents/`, and keep its raw output.
2. A comparison, posted as a comment on this record, that sorts each finding into one of three buckets:
   - already covered by harness-health (name the harness-health check);
   - already covered by the model-version prompting checklist in `docs/skill-authoring.md`;
   - genuinely new.
3. For each genuinely new finding, take exactly one of two routes:
   - a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body, either fixing the flagged instruction or extending harness-health or the checklist to catch that class;
   - a stated reason, in the comment, why it is not worth acting on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/prompt-audit` has been run once over the targets in Deliverable 1. The comment states the Claude Code version used and the target set actually covered.
- Every finding in the run's output appears in the comparison comment under exactly one of the three buckets.
- Every genuinely new finding has either a linked filed backlog record or a stated reason for no action; none is left unrouted.
- The comment states whether `/prompt-audit` reached the `plugin/skills/` library, since harness-health does not.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of Claude Code's `/prompt-audit` against claude-tweaks' own harness-health audit.

## Technical Approach

Run `/prompt-audit` from an interactive session at the repo root. Then work through its findings against two references: harness-health's analysis criteria (`plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`, the shared judge procedure) and the model-version checklist. Fixes to individual skills are not made in this record; they are filed as follow-ups so each lands with its own conformance-test run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — the existing audit whose coverage is compared
- `plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` — harness-health's shared judge procedure
- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — the manual model-version prompting checklist (line 215)
- `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md` — the levers that checklist audits against

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `/prompt-audit` can be run on demand in this environment and accepts the `plugin/` subtree as a target. It is a built-in slash command, so a headless agent may not be able to invoke it the same way. Confirm before relying on an unattended run.
- Fixing a flagged skill instruction here would touch shipped prose that conformance tests pin repo-wide (`tests/` byte-pins skill text). That is why fixes go to follow-up records, each with its own full-suite run.
- harness-health's own scope is `.claude/` by design. A finding that it misses on `plugin/skills/` is a scope question, not automatically a harness-health defect.

## Original request

Run /prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md and skills

Current State:
- Claude Code's /prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, flagging instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules.
- claude-tweaks ships a large skill library that has not been audited against the new Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 models this way.
- claude-tweaks' own harness-health skill does a related but not identical audit.

Deliverables:
- Run /prompt-audit prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own repo.
- Compare its findings against what harness-health already catches; fold in anything harness-health misses.

Acceptance Criteria:
- /prompt-audit run once with findings reviewed.
- Any genuinely new findings (not already covered by harness-health) turned into follow-up fixes or a harness-health improvement.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog#2-1-283

## Current State

#2741 added `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js`. Its `measureAgentToolCost(repoRoot)` (lines 81-98) reads each `agents/{name}.md`'s `tools:` frontmatter and returns `[]` when no `agents/` directory exists. The function is exported (`:149`) and covered by `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js`, but nothing in production calls it. `grep -rln measureAgentToolCost plugin tests` returns only the module itself and its unit test.

`estimateHarnessCost(repoRoot)` (`:120-133`) builds its `entries` from `measureSkillToolCost` alone and returns `{ entries, totalSkills, unscopedCount }`. That function is the one consumed by `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` (header comment `:18-19`: `entries` is "every skill's" record) and by `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s Harness cost-efficiency check (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md:96-101`, which runs that CLI every firing).

The documentation advertises more than is reported. `docs/plugin-structure.md:23` says harness-cost.js measures each shipped skill's `allowed-tools:` count "(and each agent definition's `tools:`)". In practice `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` (`tools: Bash`) never appears in any report. #2741's own deliverables named subagents ("so bloated skill or subagent definitions are visible"), so this is unmet scope, not a deliberate omission. The v6.134.0 release review found it (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents).

## Deliverables

1. Make `estimateHarnessCost` include agent definitions via `measureAgentToolCost`, with each entry distinguishable from skill entries (for example a `kind: 'skill' | 'agent'` field). Agent entries carry `tools`, `toolCount` and `overageRatio`. Size the agent file's bytes the same way skills are sized; shared-citation depth can be `null` or omitted for agents if it does not apply. Add an agent count to the summary alongside `totalSkills`.
2. Update `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` so its output and `flagHighToolCount` handling cover agent entries. A high-tool-count agent can then be flagged the same way a skill is.
3. Update `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s cost-efficiency check prose (`SKILL.md:96-101`) to say agents are reported alongside skills.
4. Reconcile `docs/plugin-structure.md:23`, and the CLI line at `:128` if it describes output shape, with what is now reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js --plugin-root plugin` output includes an entry for the `qa-agent` agent definition, marked as an agent rather than a skill.
- A test in `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js` fails if `estimateHarnessCost` stops including agent entries. Prove it goes red by removing the agent wiring.
- A fixture with no `agents/` directory still produces a valid report with zero agent entries and no error.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

The harness cost report now includes subagent tool scopes alongside skills, as its documentation already claimed.

## Technical Approach

Concatenate `measureAgentToolCost(repoRoot)` results into `estimateHarnessCost`'s entries with a `kind` discriminator, then sort the combined list by bytes as today. Check every consumer of `entries` (the report CLI and any test fixtures pinning the JSON shape) before changing the shape. The change is additive, so existing skill-entry fields stay identical.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js` — `estimateHarnessCost`: include agent entries with a `kind` field and an agent summary count
- `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` — report and flag agent entries; update the output-shape header comment
- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — cost-efficiency check prose (96-101)
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — reconcile lines 23 and 128 with the reported shape
- `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js` — agent-inclusion and no-agents-directory tests

## Gotchas

- `agents/` is a flat directory of `{name}.md` files, unlike `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`. Do not reuse `measuredBytes(path.join(dir, name, 'SKILL.md'))` for agents.
- `totalSkills` keeps meaning skills only. Add a separate agent count rather than changing its meaning, since harness-health's prose and any downstream reader treat it as a skill tally.
- `MINIMAL_BASELINE_TOOLS` was calibrated as a skill baseline. Note in the report or docs whether the same four-tool baseline is meaningful for agents (`qa-agent` declares `Bash` only) rather than implying an equivalence nobody validated.

## Original request

harness-cost: measureAgentToolCost is never wired into the report, though docs say agent tools: are measured

## Current State

`#2741` added `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js`. `measureAgentToolCost` (line ~81) is implemented, exported and unit-tested, but has no production caller: `estimateHarnessCost` — the only function `bin/harness-cost-report.js` and harness-health's cost-efficiency check consume — maps over `measureSkillToolCost` alone. `docs/plugin-structure.md:23` says the module measures "each agent definition's `tools:`" and is called at runtime, so the agent half is advertised but never reported; `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` (`tools: Bash`) is never measured. #2741's Deliverables name subagents ("so bloated skill or subagent definitions are visible"), so this is unmet scope, not a deliberate omission. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents, refutation not-refuted; ledger row 6).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `estimateHarnessCost` (or the report CLI) includes agent definitions' `tools:` cost via `measureAgentToolCost`, distinguishable from skill entries
- [ ] harness-health's cost-efficiency check reports agent entries alongside skills
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s description matches what is actually reported

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3047

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:test`'s pipeline path with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:70`) selects QA stories by `source_files` ∩ `node bin/verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}`. `--changed-files` (`plugin/bin/verify.js:156`, `changedFilesMode`) resolves its base through `resolveBase` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js:54`) with this precedence: `--base` first, then the checkout's own verification-stamp anchor whenever it is usable and not equal to HEAD (`:62-77`), and only then the `--integration-branch` merge-base (`:78-84`).

In a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the stamp. Bookkeeping commits follow (for example `/stories` committing a new story YAML), so by the time `/test` selects stories the stamp anchor is an ancestor of HEAD but not HEAD. The changed-file set is then only the post-stamp bookkeeping, never the build's own source changes. Observed (reporter, plugin 6.136.0): the set was a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in it, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components. The reporter selected stories by hand against `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`.

The stamp anchor is the right base for re-running tests (`affected`, `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table): the stamp records what was already verified. It is the wrong base for QA story selection, because the stamp says nothing about QA. `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md:9` reads the same `--changed-files` set to decide which files the design CLI gate judges, so it has the same blind spot.

## Deliverables

1. Add an opt-in `--ignore-stamp` flag to `verify.js --changed-files` (parsed in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js`, honored by `changedFilesMode`/`resolveBase`). It skips the stamp anchor and resolves the base from `--base` or the `--integration-branch` merge-base, keeping the existing exit-1 and `warning: resolved base equals HEAD` semantics. Reject it outside `--changed-files` the way the other read-only flags are rejected.
2. Switch `test/SKILL.md`'s pipeline QA story selection (`:70`) to `verify.js --changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}`, so selection compares story `source_files` against the run's own branch diff.
3. Switch `test/design-gate.md:9`'s `<changed-files>` resolution to the same `--ignore-stamp` form.
4. Leave `/claude-tweaks:test affected` (test re-runs) and `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping unchanged — they keep the stamp-anchored set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stamp anchored at commit A, a later source commit B, and a bookkeeping commit C on HEAD, `verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}` still returns only C's files, and `--changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}` returns B's and C's files (the merge-base diff). Both cases are covered in `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` and/or `cli.test.js`.
- `--ignore-stamp` with no resolvable `--base`/`--integration-branch` base exits 1 with a message, never an empty list.
- `--ignore-stamp` combined with a non-`--changed-files` mode is a usage error (exit 2), covered by `args.test.js`.
- `test/SKILL.md`'s QA selection and `design-gate.md` both name the `--ignore-stamp` form; the `affected` mode does not.
- The existing `verify` suites (`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/*.test.js`) pass.

## Release Note

Select pipeline QA stories against the run's full branch diff, so a build's own UI changes are never skipped because a verification stamp was written before them.

## Technical Approach

An additive flag keeps every existing `--changed-files` caller's behavior unchanged. Flipping the default would change the `affected`/`--scope` semantics that rely on the stamp anchor. The alternative of passing `--base $(git merge-base …)` from the skill prose was rejected: that hand-rolls merge-base resolution (`preferOriginRef`, degenerate-base handling) that `resolveBase` already owns.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — parse and validate `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — pass the flag through `changedFilesMode`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` — `resolveBase` skips the stamp anchor when asked
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — QA story selection uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md` — design-gate changed-file set uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` — stamp-anchored vs ignore-stamp base cases
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/args.test.js` — flag validation

## Gotchas

- `verify.js`'s usage string (`args.js:14`) and `verification.md`'s `--changed-files` description must name the new flag. Grep for every `--changed-files` mention in `plugin/skills/` before finishing (`test/SKILL.md`, `test/design-gate.md`, `test/verification.md`).
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/snippet-conformance.test.js` does not currently pin the `--changed-files` snippet. Run the full `npm test` anyway, because other conformance suites pin `test/SKILL.md` prose repo-wide.
- The reporter's alternative base (the run's materialize commit's parent) was not chosen. The integration-branch merge-base is already resolvable by `verify.js` without run-dir knowledge, and on a pr-first branch it is the same diff.

## Original request

test: pipeline QA story selection reads only post-stamp changes, so it can skip the build's own UI change

**Component:** claude-tweaks `skills/test` (pipeline QA selection) + `bin/verify.js --changed-files`
**Kind:** gap

## What happened

Inside a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the verification pass stamp. `/stories` then commits a new story YAML, and `/test` (with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present) selects stories by `source_files ∩ verify.js --changed-files`. Because `--changed-files` resolves its base to the stamp's `fullSha` whenever that sha is an ancestor of HEAD, the set at that point is only the post-stamp commits — here a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in that one-file set, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components.

## Expected

The pipeline's QA selection should compare story `source_files` against the run's own change set (the branch diff from its merge-base / the run's materialize base), not against "changes since the last verification stamp", which in a pipeline is almost always just the bookkeeping that follows `/build`.

## Workaround used

Selected stories manually against the branch diff (`git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`) and logged the deviation to `decisions.md`.

## Suggested fix

Give `/test`'s pipeline selection its own base (the run's materialize commit's parent, or `--integration-branch` merge-base) instead of the stamp-anchored `--changed-files`, or add a `--since-base` mode to `verify.js --changed-files` that ignores the stamp.


_Filed from a recommender-system `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` run (record #1207, plugin 6.136.0)._

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2806, #3017, #3063, #3066, #3113, #3129

## Current State

`.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` may declare `checks.tests` as a map of suite name to command. `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js:57-59` parses that map form (`isPlainObject(checks.tests)`) into per-suite commands plus `decl.suites`. The string form (`:53-56`) declares a single `tests` suite.

`plugin/bin/verify.js`'s `--scope` block never runs the map form's commands:

- The check set is always `parsed.cmds` (command-line `--cmd`s) filtered by the selection (`verify.js:308-313`). Only tool-scoped mode synthesizes a check from the declaration, and only from the string form (`decl.checks.tests.replace(/\{base\}/g, …)`, `:314-319`).
- The H2 check (`:321-338`) makes any required suite without a matching `--cmd` a usage error: `--scope: mode {mode} requires --cmd for: …`.

`plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` adds two more constraints:

- `:98` "at least one --cmd <name>=<command> is required", even under `--scope`.
- `:114` `--cmd-env` that "names no declared --cmd". A suite declared in `verify-scope.json` does not count.

Reported use case (plugin 6.136.0): a project declaring five suites (`tests`, `ui-static`, `ui-unit`, `ui-build`, `ui-e2e`) needed one environment variable on one suite for a full-scope re-verify. Passing one `--cmd` failed H2 for the other four. `--cmd-env` on a declared-only suite failed `:114`. The working invocation re-typed all five commands from the declaration. Two copies of each command can then drift, and the command-line copy silently wins.

## Deliverables

1. Under `--scope` with a map-form `checks.tests`, build the check set from the declaration. Each selected suite runs its declared command unless a `--cmd` with the same name overrides it. `types` and `lint` follow the same rule from `checks.types` and `checks.lint` when declared.
2. Narrow H2 so it fires only for a required name that has neither a declared command nor a `--cmd`.
3. Let `--cmd-env <suite>=KEY=VALUE` attach to a declared suite even when no `--cmd` names it. Keep the "names no check" error for names that are neither declared nor passed.
4. Relax `args.js`'s "at least one --cmd" rule when `--scope` is given and the declaration supplies checks.
5. Update the `verify.js` usage text and `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` examples that show the long `--cmd` list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `verify.js --scope <map-form declaration>` with no `--cmd` runs exactly the suites the selection picks, using their declared commands, and writes the same pass stamp a fully spelled-out invocation writes today. A test asserts the spawned command strings.
- `--cmd <suite>=<other>` overrides that one suite's declared command, and the run report names the override.
- `--cmd-env ui-e2e=FOO=1` with no `--cmd ui-e2e` sets `FOO=1` for that suite's spawn, flaky retry included.
- A string-form or absent `checks.tests`, and any invocation without `--scope`, behaves exactly as today. `tests/bin-lib/verify/args.test.js`, `scope.test.js` and `cli.test.js` pass unchanged except where they assert the removed errors, and each such edit is named in the PR.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Scoped verification now runs the test commands declared in your verify-scope file, so you no longer have to repeat every command on the command line to change one.

## Technical Approach

Make the declaration the default source of commands and `--cmd` an override layer: merge `decl`'s per-suite commands with `parsed.cmds` by name (command line wins), then filter by the selection as today. H2 and the `--cmd-env` binding then check against the merged set rather than `parsed.cmds` alone. The tool-scoped string-form path is unchanged.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — `--scope` check-set build (`:308-319`) merges declared commands; H2 (`:321-338`) checks the merged set; usage text
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — `:98` at-least-one-`--cmd` relaxed under `--scope`; `:114` `--cmd-env` binding accepts declared suites, resolved where the declaration is available
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — map-form parse (`:57-59`); reference, exposes per-suite commands
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — invocation examples
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js` — no-`--cmd` map-form run, override, `--cmd-env` on declared suite

## Gotchas

- #2806 (ready, in flight with `bot:in-progress` and an open PR) restructures `args.js`'s four-mode `parseArgs` with "no change to verify.js's CLI-facing behavior". This record changes that behavior in the same file. Build after #2806 merges, or rebase onto it, to avoid a conflicting parallel rewrite of `parseArgs`.
- `args.js` validates `--cmd-env` before the declaration is read. Binding to declared suites needs the check moved after declaration load (in `verify.js`) or the declared names passed in. Do not read the declaration file twice.
- A command-line override that silently shadows a declared command was the original drift risk. The run report must name every override so the shadowing is visible.
- The pass stamp's `suitesRun` must list the suites actually run, declared or overridden, so a later `--stamp-status` reads the same coverage as today's spelled-out run.

## Original request

bin/verify.js --scope: a map-shaped verify-scope.json's per-suite commands are never run, so every selected suite must be re-typed as `--cmd`, and `--cmd-env` can attach only to those

**Summary:** `verify-scope.json` can declare `checks.tests` as a map of suite name to command. `declaration.js` parses and validates that map, and `verify.js` uses the suite names for selection, but it never runs the declared commands. Under `--scope`, a full-mode selection requires a `--cmd` for every declared suite ("`--scope: mode full requires --cmd for: ...`"). The caller therefore re-types, on the command line, every command the declaration already holds. `--cmd-env` binds only to a command-line `--cmd`, so setting one environment variable for one suite still means re-passing all of them.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/verify.js` (the `--scope` block: the check-set filter at ~L308-320 and the H2 required-names check at ~L327-338), `bin/lib/verify/args.js` (the "at least one --cmd" rule and the `--cmd-env` → `--cmd` binding)

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

**Related:** #2806 untangles `parseArgs` with "No change to verify.js's CLI-facing behavior", so it explicitly leaves this behaviour alone. #3017 covers only relative `--scope` resolving against the process cwd. #2779 (closed) added `--cmd-env` and made "names no declared --cmd" an error on purpose. None of them covers the coupling below.

## Current State

- `declaration.js` turns `checks.tests` (map form) into `decl.checks.tests = {suite: command}` and `decl.suites = [...]`.
- `verify.js` reads `decl.checks.tests` only in tool-scoped mode, and only for the string form (`decl.checks.tests.replace(/\{base\}/g, ...)`). The map form's commands are never spawned. The check set is always `parsed.cmds` filtered by the selection.
- The H2 check makes a missing `--cmd` for any required suite a usage error, so a full run must pass every suite.
- `args.js` rejects a `--cmd-env <name>=...` whose name has no command-line `--cmd`. A declared suite does not count.

**Use case (plugin 6.136.0):** a project declares five suites (`tests`, `ui-static`, `ui-unit`, `ui-build`, `ui-e2e`), each with its full command in `verify-scope.json`. A full-scope re-verify that needed one environment variable on one suite cost several retries:
1. Passing only the one `--cmd` it wanted to tweak produced `mode full requires --cmd for: <the other four>`.
2. `--cmd-env` aimed at a suite taken from the declaration produced `names no declared --cmd`.
3. The working invocation re-typed all five commands from the declaration onto the command line. Two copies of each command can now drift, and when they do, the command-line copy silently wins.

Expected: the declaration is the source of truth for a declared suite's command. `--cmd` overrides it only when given, and `--cmd-env` can target any declared suite.

## Deliverables

1. Under `--scope` with a map-form `checks.tests`, build the check set from the declaration. Each selected suite runs its declared command unless a `--cmd` with the same name overrides it. `types` and `lint` follow the same rule from `checks.types` and `checks.lint` when declared.
2. Narrow the H2 required-names check so it fires only for a required name that has neither a declared command nor a `--cmd`.
3. Let `--cmd-env <suite>=KEY=VALUE` attach to a declared suite even when no `--cmd` names it. Keep the "names no check" error for names that are neither declared nor passed.
4. Relax `args.js`'s "at least one --cmd is required" when `--scope` is given, since the declaration supplies the checks. Coordinate with #2806, which restructures the same parser.
5. Update the usage text and the verification docs that show the long `--cmd` list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `verify.js --scope <map-form declaration>` with no `--cmd` runs exactly the suites the selection picks, using their declared commands, and writes the same stamp a fully spelled-out invocation writes today.
- `--cmd <suite>=<other>` overrides that one suite's declared command, and the run report names the override.
- `--cmd-env ui-e2e=FOO=1` with no `--cmd ui-e2e` sets `FOO=1` for that suite's spawn, flaky retry included.
- A string-form or absent `checks.tests`, and any invocation without `--scope`, behaves exactly as it does today, and the existing args and scope tests pass unchanged except where they assert the removed errors.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Three `bin/` CLIs resolve repo-relative inputs against `process.cwd()`. When the shell sits in a subdirectory of the checkout, they silently produce plausible-looking wrong results:

- **`bin/verify.js --scope`**: `readDeclaration(parsed.scope)` (`plugin/bin/verify.js:244`) reads the path as given. `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js:22-27` maps `ENOENT` to `{ ok: true, decl: null, missing: true }`, so a relative `--scope` that misses because of the cwd reads as "no declaration" and the run falls back to the full suite. `--cwd` (`verify.js:374`) is applied to the check commands only, never to the `--scope` path.
- **`bin/wrap-up-engine.js plan`**: `gatherFacts({ cwd: process.cwd(), ... })` (`plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js:194-196`) evaluates fact gates (journeys, CLAUDE.md sections) against the cwd. The same `process.cwd()` pattern recurs at `:291`, `:318`, `:468` and `:634`. `:467` already computes `resolveRepoRoot(process.cwd())` for one path.
- **`bin/build-review-context.js build`**: `plugin/bin/lib/review-context/build.js:58-73` reads each changed file as `readFile(f)` with the repo-relative name from `git diff --name-only`. From a subdirectory every read fails and every file lands in `emptySections`.

Reported run (plugin 6.136.0, cwd `<worktree>/web`): verify.js printed `Scope: full — no declaration at .claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and ran an unscoped 22-minute suite. `plan` reported "no journeys" although `docs/journeys/` exists at the root, and flagged a CLAUDE.md change the diff never made. build-review-context reported all 26 changed files as empty sections. An absolute `--scope` path, or running from the root, gave correct results.

## Deliverables

1. **verify.js**: resolve a relative `--scope` against the checkout root, which is `--cwd` when given, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the process cwd. An explicitly passed `--scope` path that does not exist after resolution is a usage error, exit 2 through the existing `scopeUsageExit` shape (`verify.js:236`), never "no declaration". Keep the missing-declaration fallback only for the implicit default path, if one exists.
2. **wrap-up-engine.js**: every subcommand that gathers repo facts resolves the repo root once (`resolveRepoRoot`, already used at `:467`) and passes it as `cwd` instead of `process.cwd()`. Each `process.cwd()` site listed above is either converted or annotated with why the raw cwd is correct there.
3. **build-review-context.js**: read per-file sections relative to the repo toplevel (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), not the cwd.
4. Each CLI's `--help` or header comment states that repo-relative inputs resolve against the checkout root.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For each of the three CLIs, a test runs it with the process cwd set to a subdirectory of a temp git repo (via `execFileSync`'s `cwd` option) and asserts the root-correct result: verify selects the declared suites, `plan` sees the root `docs/journeys/`, and `build` writes non-empty sections. Prove each test goes red against today's code.
- A test asserts `verify.js --scope does-not-exist.json` exits 2 with a message naming the resolved path.
- Running each CLI from the repo root produces byte-identical output to today. Existing suites under `tests/bin-lib/verify/`, `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/`, `tests/bin-lib/review-context/`, `tests/wrap-up-engine-run-dir-anchoring.test.js` and `tests/wrap-up-engine-journey-crlf.test.js` pass.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Verification, wrap-up planning and review-context building now give correct results when run from a subfolder of your project, instead of silently running everything or seeing nothing.

## Technical Approach

Resolve the root once per invocation at the CLI boundary and thread it down as an explicit `cwd`/`root` argument. The libraries already accept one (`gatherFacts({cwd})`, `verify`'s `--cwd`). Prefer `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` over walking up for a marker file, so a linked worktree resolves to its own root, not the main checkout. Changing exit 0 to exit 2 on a missing explicit `--scope` is a deliberate behavior change: a typo'd path must stop the run rather than widen it.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — `--scope` resolution against `--cwd`/toplevel (`:235-276`); explicit-missing → exit 2
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — `readDeclaration` (`:22-27`) missing-file result, distinguishing explicit from implicit callers if needed
- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` — `process.cwd()` sites (`:194`, `:291`, `:318`, `:468`, `:634`) → resolved repo root
- `plugin/bin/lib/review-context/build.js` — per-file `readFile(f)` (`:58-73`) relative to the toplevel
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js` — subdirectory-cwd and missing-explicit-scope cases
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-plan.test.js` — subdirectory-cwd fact-gate case
- `tests/bin-lib/review-context/build.test.js` — subdirectory-cwd section case

## Gotchas

- `/claude-tweaks:test`'s and `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s prose may pass `--scope` as a relative path today. After this change that path resolves against the root instead of the cwd, which is the intended fix, but grep the skills for `--scope` call sites and confirm none relied on cwd-relative resolution from a non-root directory.
- `wrap-up-engine.js:584` reads `readRunState(args.runDir)?.worktree || process.cwd()`. The run-state worktree is already the right root there. Do not override it with the main checkout's toplevel.
- A file deleted in the diff legitimately has no content to read. It must still land in `emptySections`, so the fix must not hide real deletions.
- Run-dir anchoring rules (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`, `[IL-127]`) are about the main checkout, not the worktree toplevel. Do not conflate the two roots when threading `cwd`.

## Original request

verify.js / wrap-up-engine.js / build-review-context.js: repo-relative inputs resolve against the process cwd, not the git toplevel or --cwd

**Summary:** Three CLIs silently degrade to plausible-looking wrong results when the shell's cwd is a subdirectory of the checkout, because they resolve repo-relative inputs against the process cwd.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/verify.js (`--scope`), bin/wrap-up-engine.js (`plan` fact gates), bin/build-review-context.js (`build` per-file sections)

**Repro steps:**
1. In a worktree whose app lives in a subdirectory (e.g. `<worktree>/web`), leave the shell cwd in that subdirectory (common after running the app's own npm scripts).
2. Run `node bin/verify.js --scope .claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json --cwd <worktree-root>`.
3. Run `node bin/wrap-up-engine.js plan --run-dir <anchored run dir> --base <sha>`.
4. Run `node bin/build-review-context.js build --base <sha> --branch HEAD`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: each CLI resolves repo-relative inputs against the git toplevel of the checkout it operates on (or `--cwd` where that flag exists), or fails loudly when an explicitly passed path does not exist.
Actual:
- verify.js prints `Scope: full — no declaration at .claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and runs the full suite (a 22-minute unscoped run here); `--scope` is resolved against the process cwd, not `--cwd`. An absolute `--scope` path selects suites correctly.
- wrap-up-engine.js `plan` evaluates fact gates against the subdirectory: "no journeys" although `docs/journeys/` exists at the repo root, and "CLAUDE.md Commands section changed" although the diff never touched CLAUDE.md. Re-running from the worktree root gives the correct gates.
- build-review-context.js lists every changed file (26) in `emptySections`; only the top-of-bundle diff has content.

Suggested fix: resolve relative `--scope`, run-dir-adjacent and per-file paths against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (honouring `--cwd` where given); treat an explicitly passed declaration path that does not exist as exit 2, not "no declaration".

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2987

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the pass stamp only for a passing run of the full resolved check set: the write gate requires `fullSet && !parsed.noStamp` (verify.js ~line 568). `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:48` requires any deliberately partial `--cmd` set to pass `--no-stamp`, because the runner cannot tell a partial set from the full one. Both rules are correct on their own.

Together they leave a long suite with no way to earn a stamp. A project whose declared checks take about 25 minutes end to end must split verification into chunks under the harness's 10-minute foreground Bash cap. Every chunk is partial, so every chunk passes `--no-stamp`, and `--stamp-status` never reads `verifiedHead: true`. Every later gate (`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5, the second call of a dispatched two-call group, skip-if-recent) then re-runs the whole set, so the two-call dispatch form pays the full ~25 minutes twice even when HEAD did not move. Agent-written stamps are forbidden (#1921), correctly, so there is no workaround. Reported on plugin 6.136.0.

Why not a single background run: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:46`'s Foreground rule already permits one full-set run with `run_in_background` when the set exceeds the 600 s foreground cap — but only for the orchestrating session. "A dispatched subagent never backgrounds it — its turn cannot wait on a notification" (the `[IL-108]` family; #1904 stalled waiting on a background verify child's notification that never arrived). `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call form runs each `/flow` call as a dispatched subagent, so inside those calls the 600 s cap is hard and chunking is the only sanctioned option. That is the case this record targets.

## Deliverables

1. A per-suite stamp mode: `verify.js --stamp-suite` (or equivalent) records, for a passing chunk, which declared checks passed against which sha and tree state, written by the runner only.
2. `--stamp-status` composes `verifiedHead: true` when every check declared in `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` (types, lint, and each declared suite) has a passing per-suite record at the current clean HEAD.
3. A per-suite record never counts toward a different sha, a dirty tree, or a check it did not run; a failing chunk clears or never writes its record.
4. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the chunked flow: when to use it, and that `--no-stamp` stays required for ad hoc partial runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Running each declared check in separate `verify.js` invocations with the per-suite mode, all passing at one clean HEAD, makes `--stamp-status` report `verifiedHead: true`.
2. If any declared check has no passing record at the current HEAD, `verifiedHead` stays `false`.
3. A per-suite record from an earlier sha, or written against a dirty tree, does not count.
4. A plain `--no-stamp` partial run still writes nothing.
5. The verify stamp tests pass, with new cases for 1–4.

## Release Note

Long test suites can now be verified in chunks under the 10-minute command limit and still earn a full verification stamp.

## Technical Approach

Store per-suite pass records alongside the existing stamp (same git-dir location, runner-written), keyed by sha and check name. Have `--stamp-status` compute the full-coverage verdict from the declared check list in `verify-scope.json`. Keep the existing full-run stamp unchanged so current callers see no difference.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — new flag, write path, and `--stamp-status` composition
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` — per-suite record read/write
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — flag parsing
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — declared check list from `verify-scope.json`
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — chunked-run documentation
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- #2806 (untangling `verify/args.js`'s parseArgs, PR #2836) is in flight on `args.js`; build this after it merges or rebase onto it.
- #2987 changes the same stamp's dirty handling; agree one stamp schema so the two compose.
- A project with no `verify-scope.json` has no declared check list to compose against; per-suite mode should refuse there with a clear message rather than guess.
- The runner stays the only stamp writer; nothing here may add an agent-side write path.

## Original request

bin/verify.js: no way to compose a full pass stamp from chunked --no-stamp runs, so a suite longer than the 10-minute foreground cap never verifies HEAD

**Summary:** A project whose declared suites take about 25 minutes end to end (a Python allowlist near 12 minutes, an e2e suite of 4-5 minutes, build plus lint of 3 minutes) must split verification into chunks under the harness's 10-minute foreground Bash timeout; every chunk is a partial `--cmd` set and must pass `--no-stamp`, so `verify.js --stamp-status` never reads `verifiedHead: true` and every later gate (review Step 1.5, the second call of a dispatched group, Skip-if-recent) re-runs the whole set.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/verify.js (pass stamp) and test/verification.md ("A targeted run never stamps")

**Use case:** verification.md is explicit that a partial `--cmd` set must pass `--no-stamp` because the runner cannot tell a partial set from the full one. That rule is correct, but it leaves a long suite with no sanctioned way to ever earn a stamp: the two-call dispatch form (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up`) pays the full ~25-minute set twice — once in the first call's chunks and again when the second call's review Step 1.5 finds `present: false` — even when HEAD did not move. Expected: a per-suite stamp mode — e.g. `--stamp-suite <name>` recording that suite's pass against the sha, with `--stamp-status` composing `verifiedHead: true` once every suite declared in `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` has a passing stamp at a clean HEAD — so chunked runs under the foreground cap can still produce a trustworthy full pass without an agent-side stamp write (which #1921 rightly forbids).

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3002

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the verification pass stamp for any passing full run regardless of tree state (the write gate "never consults dirty", verify.js ~line 547), and `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true` only when the stored stamp was recorded against a clean tree at the current HEAD (`stampCoversCleanHead`, verify.js ~line 125). The dirty value comes from `gitInfo()` in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js`.

When a check regenerates a tracked file — the reported case is a Next.js production build rewriting `next-env.d.ts` — the tree is dirty at stamp time even though every check passed on the exact HEAD commit. `--stamp-status` then reads `verifiedHead: false`, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 re-triggers `/claude-tweaks:test`, and the re-run dirties the tree again. The only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out, or a manual restore-and-restamp.

A second, smaller gap from the same report: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` gives no guidance for a `--cmd` that needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path; the reporter needed two failed runs to learn that a committed wrapper script must put the working directory first on the import path.

## Deliverables

1. `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` accepts a `generated` list of path globs. `verify.js`'s dirty computation for the pass stamp ignores changes to paths matching those globs; any other dirty path still disqualifies the stamp exactly as today.
2. The stamp records which declared-generated paths were dirty at stamp time, so the exemption is auditable.
3. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the `generated` key (when to use it, and that it must name only files the checks regenerate) and adds a short note on `--cmd` wrappers needing environment variables or a working-directory-first import path.
4. `/claude-tweaks:init`'s verify-scope starter (`plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js`) accepts the new key without breaking existing scope files.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full passing run whose only dirty path matches a declared `generated` glob produces a stamp for which `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true`, and the stamp lists that path.
2. A full passing run with any other dirty path still produces `verifiedHead: false`.
3. A scope file without `generated` behaves exactly as today.
4. `node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` and the verify CLI tests pass, with new cases for 1–3.

## Release Note

Verification can now earn a passing stamp when a check regenerates a declared generated file, instead of forcing a second run.

## Technical Approach

Extend the verify-scope declaration parser to read `generated`, pass the globs into the dirty computation used for the pass stamp (not the general report's `dirty`, which other readers may rely on), and record the exempted paths in the stamp. Option (b) from the original request — exempting any path that was clean before the run and dirtied by it — is rejected: a check that rewrites source (a formatter or `lint --fix`) would then vouch for a tree that differs from HEAD. Explicit declaration keeps that case disqualifying.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — stamp write and `--stamp-status` dirty handling
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — `gitInfo()` dirty computation; add a filtered variant for the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` — record exempted generated paths in the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — parse `generated` from `verify-scope.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js` — starter scope file compatibility
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — document `generated` and the `--cmd` wrapper note
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- #2806 (untangling `verify/args.js`'s parseArgs, PR #2836) is in flight in the same module family; land after it merges or rebase onto it to avoid conflicts.
- #3002 (per-suite stamps for chunked runs) changes the same stamp format; coordinate the stamp schema so both additions compose.
- The stamp's existing semantics (#1921: the runner is the only writer; #1784: no agent-side writes) must not change.

## Original request

bin/verify.js pass stamp: reads dirty when a check regenerates a tracked file

**Component:** `bin/verify.js` pass stamp (`--stamp-status`, `verifiedHead`) and `test/verification.md` "Verification pass stamp", plugin version 6.134.1.

**Kind:** Gap.

**What happened.** A project's full check list includes a production build of a Next.js app. That build rewrites a tracked, generated type-declaration file (`next-env.d.ts`) in place, so the working tree is dirty at the moment `verify.js` writes its pass stamp. Every check passed on the exact HEAD commit, but `--stamp-status` then reports `verifiedHead: false`, and `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 treats `TEST_PASSED=true` plus a non-verifying stamp as "re-trigger `/claude-tweaks:test`". Re-running the same full set dirties the tree again, so the only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out.

**Why it matters.** The stamp's dirty rule exists to stop a pass on uncommitted source from vouching for a commit. A file the checks themselves regenerate is a different case, and today it forces a redundant run (minutes of wall-clock per review) or a manual restore-and-rerun on every project whose build touches a tracked generated file.

**Suggested behaviour.** One of: (a) let `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` declare `generated` paths the stamp's dirty check ignores; (b) have `verify.js` compare the dirty set before and after the run and treat paths that were clean before the run and dirtied only by the checks as non-disqualifying, recording them in the stamp; or (c) document the workaround in `test/verification.md` (restore the generated file, then re-stamp with a check set that does not regenerate it).

**Second, related observation from the same run.** A project with no `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and a Python test list that needs environment variables has no documented way to express `--cmd tests=` other than a hand-written wrapper script, and a script-driven test runner resolves the project's packages differently from `python -m pytest` (the script's directory, not the working directory, is first on the import path). A short note in `test/verification.md` — "when `--cmd` needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path, commit a wrapper in the project and put the working directory first on the import path" — would have saved two failed verification runs.

## Current State

In recommendation mode, `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md`'s Step 0.5 (lines 79-103) counts a journey as **affected** when any of its `files:` frontmatter entries appears in the changed-file set (step 2, line 86). For each affected journey it then renders `> Recommended follow-up: /claude-tweaks:visual-review journey:{…}` (line 100). Nothing checks whether the change, or the journey, has a browser-renderable surface.

On #2769's review this produced a false recommendation. `plugin/bin/lib/gif/palette.js`, a CLI and agent-only module, is listed in `docs/journeys/walkthrough-gif-capture-2758.md`'s `files:` (line 8), so Step 0.5 recommended a browser walk of a journey that has no page to open. A patch fixing this was staged and approved in run `2026-10-03T110711-record-2769`. By then that run's branch had already auto-merged, so the patch was reverted rather than orphaned.

`plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` already defines the frontend-surface signal this needs. Layer 2 (line 68) covers the materialized body-metadata `Surface:` header. Layer 3 (line 5) is the file-extension sniff fallback.

## Deliverables

1. In Step 0.5, gate the "affected journey" verdict on a frontend-surface signal as well as the `files:` overlap. A journey counts as affected only when the run carries a frontend surface per `frontend-detection.md`'s precedence: a materialized `Surface: web|mobile|desktop` (Layer 2), or, when no `Surface:` is present, a UI trigger file in the changed-file set (Layer 3). Cite that file's precedence rather than restating it.
2. When the overlap exists but the surface signal does not, return the existing no-recommendation line, or a variant that names the suppressed journeys and the reason. Never return the `Recommended follow-up` line in that case.
3. Before writing the prose, re-derive the heuristic against a typical consumer web app. In a project whose journeys are mostly browser-navigable, check that a backend-only change touching a journey's `files:` does not suppress a recommendation a human would want, such as an API change behind a visible page. Record the conclusion in `## Gotchas` of the build's plan or the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A run whose changed files overlap a journey's `files:` but which has no frontend-surface signal (`Surface: backend|infra|terminal`, or no UI trigger file when no `Surface:` is present) does not render a `Recommended follow-up: /claude-tweaks:visual-review journey:` line from Step 0.5.
- A run with `Surface: web` (or a UI trigger file) and a `files:` overlap renders the same recommendation table and follow-up line as today.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Visual review no longer recommends a browser walkthrough when a change only touches non-UI code.

## Technical Approach

This is a prose change in `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md`, steps 2 and 4 of Step 0.5. The parent (`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6 code-only) already passes the changed-file list, so the build should also have the parent pass the materialized surface. Alternatively, Step 0.5 can read `Surface:` from the run's materialized header the same way the design wrapper does. Pick whichever needs no new plumbing, and say which in the PR. Recover the staged patch from the archived run, `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/2026-10-03T110711-record-2769/staged/wrap-up-skill-1.md`, if it is still present. Use it as a starting point, not as settled text.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md` — Step 0.5 (79-103): gate "affected" on a frontend-surface signal
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` — read-only: Layer 2/3 precedence to cite
- `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md` — check what Step 6 code-only passes to recommendation mode; extend it if the surface value is needed

## Gotchas

- Do not fix this by pruning `palette.js` from the journey's `files:`. That entry is legitimate journey traceability, and `docs/journeys/` hygiene belongs to `/journey-health`, not this record.
- The consumer-project check in deliverable 3 is a real risk to address, not a box to tick. A web app's backend change can still break a page, which is why the gate keys on the run's surface rather than on each changed file's extension alone.

missing rows before it could flip `review` to checked (logged in this run's `decisions.md` at
21:59:13). Nothing caught the drift before that point — there is no code or test pinning this
specific composition rule, unlike, e.g., the `tests/wrap-up-registry-pin.test.js` pattern used
elsewhere in this plugin to keep a documented table and its implementation from drifting.

Evidence: record #2749's run, `decisions.md` entries at 21:58:02 (discovery) and 21:59:13
(self-heal), PR #2875's body history (`gh pr view 2875 --json body`). Cost this session: one
extra read-patch-write round trip to detect and self-heal the missing rows before the review
phase-exit checklist flip could proceed — low, but would compound across every two-call dispatch

Surface: infra

## Current State

When a feature run finishes, none of its closing surfaces tell the human how to use or check what was built: which page to open, which steps to take, what result to expect. The filed use case was a four-spec `/flow` bundle that merged and deployed in one session. The user then had to ask in chat what had been completed and how to use it.

Verified against the tree:

- `plugin/skills/flow/summary-template.md` has these sections: Spec, Timing, Key Outputs, Manual Steps Required, Actions Performed, Creative Opportunities, Depth Opportunities and Next Actions (lines 10-87). `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-summary.md` has Timing, Manual Steps Required and Per-Spec Details (lines 8-39). Neither template has a section aimed at the user, and nothing anywhere in `plugin/skills/` renders a walkthrough of how to use the result.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md:52-80` makes the non-parent Verification Brief depend on `exceedsOversightFloor` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/oversight-floor.js`, #367). On `exceeds: false` it skips Steps 1-4: no `demo:pending`, no observation plan, no brief. `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md:228-238` applies the same risk-only gate on the parent path. Part 2 of that brief, the walkthrough of the primary path, is the only walkthrough aimed at a human, so a run below the floor gets none.
- `plugin/skills/demo/SKILL.md` Step 2 (lines 78-166) runs Prepare/Validate/Show from the brief's `### Observation plan`. The user found that output reads like an agent procedure.

## Deliverables

1. **One shared "Try it" block.** Define a single shared shape for a human walkthrough of each feature: precondition (deployed? data sync? feature flag?), access tier or login, entry point (route, page or command), steps, and expected result. Build it from the spec's Deliverables and Acceptance Criteria plus the QA stories that passed. For a non-web surface, use the observation plan's Entry point command instead of a route. Put it in one place (a new `_shared/` contract, or `_shared/observation-plan.md` if it fits there) and have every consumer cite it rather than copy it.
2. **Pipeline summaries.** `flow/summary-template.md` gets a mandatory `### Try it` section for each spec. `flow/multispec-summary.md` gets one section per spec plus a section for the end-to-end path across specs.
3. **Walkthrough no longer depends on the oversight floor.** In both `wrap-up/verification-brief.md` and `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`, the floor continues to gate the `demo:pending` label and the sign-off ceremony only. The walkthrough is produced on every feature delivery, including runs below the floor, where it appears in the summary or PR without a full brief.
4. **Demo shows the walkthrough first.** `/claude-tweaks:demo` renders the same Try it content at the top of its Show step, before Prepare/Validate output. That way `/demo #N` and the pipeline summary always present the same walkthrough.
5. Update the `node --test` prose suites that pin these templates or the floor-gate wording in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `/flow` run on a record below the oversight floor (`exceedsOversightFloor` returns `exceeds: false`) still ends with a `### Try it` section in its Pipeline Summary, and that section names an entry point, steps and an expected result.
- A multi-spec run's summary has one Try it section per spec plus one section for the end-to-end path.
- A record below the floor still gets no `demo:pending` label and no sign-off ceremony, so floor-gating of the label is unchanged.
- `/claude-tweaks:demo #N` on a record whose brief has a Try it block shows that block before any Prepare/Validate output.
- The Try it shape is defined in exactly one file. `flow/summary-template.md`, `flow/multispec-summary.md`, `wrap-up/verification-brief.md` and `demo/SKILL.md` cite it and do not restate its fields.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Finished feature runs now end with a "Try it" walkthrough that says where to go, what to do and what to expect, even for low-risk changes.

## Technical Approach

Start with the shared block, because the other three surfaces depend on it. Most of its content already exists in the green QA stories (URL, steps, assertions) and in the spec's ACs, so the block is mostly a human-readable rendering of evidence already produced, not a new data source. Next, split the floor gate in `verification-brief.md`: one decision for the walkthrough (always) and one for `demo:pending` plus sign-off (gated). Keep the #2383 `oversightExempt` recording unchanged, because that tracks the label and not the walkthrough. Change the summary templates and demo's Show step last.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/summary-template.md` — add the mandatory `### Try it` section for each spec
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-summary.md` — add Try it sections per spec plus an end-to-end path section
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md` — split the oversight-floor gate (walkthrough always; label and ceremony gated)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — same split on the parent path
- `plugin/skills/demo/SKILL.md` — Show step renders the Try it block first
- `plugin/skills/_shared/observation-plan.md` — candidate home for the shared Try it shape, or the new `_shared/` file cites it
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/oversight-floor.js` — read-only; its semantics do not change

## Gotchas

- This touches four skill surfaces. If the builder finds it larger than one agent-sized change, split it at the shared block: the shared shape plus the summary templates first, then the verification-brief gate split and the demo change.
- Do not remove the floor gate on `demo:pending`. The gate is correct for the ceremony. What the record objects to is only that it also hides the walkthrough.
- A run with no green QA stories (a backend or infra surface) still needs a Try it block. Build it from the ACs and an observation-plan Entry point command, and never leave it empty or render it as placeholder text.
- `/claude-tweaks:demo`'s legacy-brief path (`demo/legacy-brief-compatibility.md`) reads briefs without an Observation plan, so keep that path working.

## Original request

flow / verification-brief / demo: a finished feature run never tells the human how to use or verify what was built

**Summary:** A finished feature run never tells the human how to use or verify what was built — the closing surfaces (multi-spec Pipeline Summary, Review Console, parent-gate Verification Brief, `/claude-tweaks:demo`) report gates, commits and console rows, not "open this page, do this, expect that".

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:flow` (summary-template.md / multispec-summary.md), `wrap-up/verification-brief.md` + `verification-brief-parent-gate.md` (oversight-floor gate), `/claude-tweaks:demo`

**Use case:**
A four-spec `/flow` bundle (data layer + three UI/AI consumers) completed, merged and deployed in one session. The user then had to ask, in chat, "tell me how I can use these new features — what did we actually complete?". Nothing the pipeline had produced answered that for a person:

- The Pipeline Summary lists build/test/review/polish outcomes, timing, manual steps and survey recommendations — nothing about the features from the user's side.
- The Review Console lists auto-applied decisions and staged patches — an audit surface, not a walkthrough.
- The parent-gate Verification Brief — the one artifact whose Part 2 is "a walkthrough of the feature's primary path" — was skipped by design: the parent's sub-issues maxed at `risk:medium` against a `risk-floor: high`, so `exceedsOversightFloor` returned false and no brief was composed. The only human-facing walkthrough is therefore gated on risk, which is the wrong trigger: a low-risk feature still needs to be found and tried by the person who asked for it.
- `/claude-tweaks:demo`'s output (Prepare/Validate/Show driven by an observation plan) reads as an agent-facing procedure; the user's verbatim assessment was "not super satisfied with the demo skill in its current output".

What the user wants, by default and independent of the oversight floor: every feature delivery ends with a human "Try it" section — per feature: the route or page to open, the login tier it needs, the steps (click/type), the expected result, and any precondition (deployed? data sync run? feature flag?). For a bundle, one section per spec plus the end-to-end path across them. `/claude-tweaks:demo` should consume and present the same walkthrough rather than a separate observation-plan shape, so the two never diverge.

**Suggested shape:**
1. `flow/summary-template.md` and `multispec-summary.md` gain a mandatory `### Try it` section (per spec: precondition, tier, route, steps, expected), composed from the spec's Deliverables/ACs plus the QA stories that passed — the stories already encode URL + steps + assertions, so the walkthrough is mostly a human-readable rendering of the green stories.
2. The parent-gate/non-parent Verification Brief's Part 2 walkthrough is produced regardless of the oversight floor; the floor should only gate the `demo:pending` label and sign-off ceremony, not the existence of the walkthrough.
3. `/claude-tweaks:demo` renders that same `Try it` content as its Show phase (and can keep Prepare/Validate as optional automation), so a human running `/demo #N` gets the walkthrough first.

## Current State

External guidance (attributed to newer-model best-practice advice) argues that skill descriptions should shrink and that pre-reading doc stacks written for older, weaker models should stop, on the premise that a more capable model needs less hand-holding prose to trigger and use a skill correctly. claude-tweaks currently has ~40+ skills, many with substantial `SKILL.md` files and multi-file lazy-loaded sub-documents (per `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s conventions), whose descriptions and content depth have not been audited against this specific guidance.

## Deliverables

Audit a representative sample of claude-tweaks' skill descriptions and frontmatter against the trimming guidance, and produce findings: which descriptions carry verbosity that no longer earns its keep for a newer model, and which genuinely need their current depth (a skill whose triggering accuracy or correctness depends on detailed disambiguation, not verbosity for its own sake). Apply trims only where the finding is clear-cut; leave ambiguous cases as documented findings for a human decision rather than trimming speculatively.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least a representative sample of skill descriptions/frontmatter (not necessarily all ~40+) is reviewed against the guidance, with findings stated per-skill (trim / keep-as-is / needs-human-judgment), not a blanket assertion.
- Any trims actually applied preserve triggering accuracy — verified by checking the trimmed description still matches this project's own skill-selection conventions (`docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Frontmatter conventions section) and doesn't remove disambiguating detail that exists for a documented reason (e.g. distinguishing near-identical skill names).
- Findings and any applied changes are summarized in the record's own closing report or a linked doc, not left implicit in a diff alone.

## Release Note

Trimmed skill descriptions that no longer help newer models pick the right skill.

## Technical Approach

Read `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Frontmatter conventions section first to understand this repo's existing description-writing rules before trimming against external guidance — the two may already agree, or the external guidance may conflict with an already-deliberate convention here, in which case that conflict itself is a finding worth stating rather than silently picking one side. Sample a cross-section of skills (a few long-description ones, a few already-terse ones) rather than attempting all ~40+ in one pass, given the record's own scope is an audit, not a mandated full rewrite.

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — this repo's existing frontmatter/description conventions, the baseline to compare external guidance against
- A sample of `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter blocks — the actual audit targets (specific files depend on which sample is chosen)

## Gotchas

- Don't trim indiscriminately — a skill's description length sometimes exists specifically to disambiguate from a near-identical skill name or to state a hard trigger condition precisely; removing that in the name of brevity could regress triggering accuracy, which is a worse outcome than the verbosity the record is trying to fix.
- If this repo's own `docs/skill-authoring.md` conventions already conflict with the external trimming guidance, surface that conflict explicitly as a finding rather than silently reconciling it one way — that's a decision for a human, not this shaping pass or the eventual build.

Context: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra guidance says to shrink skill descriptions and stop pre-reading doc stacks written for older, weaker models.

Scope: Audit claude-tweaks' own skill descriptions and templates against this trimming guidance.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md:294` runs `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"` in the open-linked-PR pass (#1224 block). That variable is not in the script's opening session-tmp `files` map (`queue-pull-script.md:17` onward), which declares every other `DISPATCH_*` path. The redirect target therefore expands to an empty string, and bash prints `: No such file or directory` on every queue pull. The script has no `set -e`/`set -u`, so execution continues. The message is noise, but it reads as a failure in every `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` run (bare drain or `#N`).

`git grep -n "DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED\|open-pr-excluded" -- plugin` returns only that one line. Nothing reads the file. #1752 moved per-reason exclusion files to the unified `dispatch-exclusions.json` (`plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js`). The open-PR pass now records exclusions via `appendExclusion(…, { reason: 'open-pr' })` into `$DISPATCH_EXCLUSIONS`, which `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s `#N`/`#N,#M` paths read. The line at `:294` is a leftover from that migration.

## Deliverables

1. Delete `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"` from `queue-pull-script.md:294`.
2. Add a conformance test to `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` asserting that every `$DISPATCH_*` variable the script references is either declared in its `files` map or assigned in the script. This guards against the same migration leftover recurring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `queue-pull-script.md` contains no reference to `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED`.
- The new test fails on the current file, naming `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED` (verify by running it before the deletion), and passes after it.
- Existing `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/` suites, and any byte-pin or snippet-conformance test over `queue-pull-script.md`, pass. Update a byte pin only if one pins this exact fence, and name it in the PR.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Dispatch no longer prints a spurious "No such file or directory" error each time it pulls the queue.

## Technical Approach

A one-line deletion plus a referenced-vs-declared scan of the script. The original request's proposed diff (preserved below) is a reasonable starting point. Its declaration regex must match the `files` map's actual `KEY: 'file'` lines and any `KEY=` assignments, and the reference regex must cover both `$VAR` and `${VAR}`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — delete the dead redirect (`:294`)
- `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` — referenced-vs-declared `$DISPATCH_*` conformance test

## Gotchas

- `queue-pull-script.md` is run verbatim by `/dispatch` Step 2, and some of its fences may be byte-pinned by snippet-conformance tests. Grep `tests/` for the file name before editing.
- `node-eval-file.js` heredoc bodies inside the script reference shell variables through `process.env` or `$VAR` interpolation. Make sure the scan does not flag a variable that is assigned inside a heredoc-fed command as undeclared, or narrow the scan to shell-level references.

## Original request

dispatch: queue-pull-script.md redirects to undeclared $DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED (": No such file or directory" on every pull)

**Summary:** queue-pull-script.md writes to the never-declared $DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED, so every queue pull prints ": No such file or directory"

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** dispatch (skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md)

**Repro steps:**
1. On any project, run `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` (bare drain or `#N`) so Step 2 runs `queue-pull-script.md` verbatim.
2. Watch the open-linked-PR pass (#1224 block).

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the open-PR pass runs silently; every `$DISPATCH_*` path the script writes is declared in its opening `files` map.
Actual: bash prints `: No such file or directory` on every queue pull. The script has no `set -e`/`set -u`, so execution continues and the error is only noise, but it reads as a failure.

**Root cause:** `skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md:294` runs `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"`. The opening `files` map (`queue-pull-script.md:17-39`) declares every `DISPATCH_*` session-tmp path except this one; it was dropped in the #1752 move to the unified `dispatch-exclusions.json` (`bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js`), so the redirect target expands to an empty string. Nothing reads it any more: it is the only occurrence of `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED`/`open-pr-excluded` in the plugin, and the open-PR pass now records exclusions via `appendExclusion(..., { reason: 'open-pr' })` into `$DISPATCH_EXCLUSIONS`, which `SKILL.md`'s `#N`/`#N,#M` paths read. A mechanical referenced-vs-declared comparison found it is the only undeclared `DISPATCH_*` variable in the script. Deleting the line is the fix.

**Proposed fix:**
```diff
diff --git a/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md b/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
--- a/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
+++ b/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
@@ -291,7 +291,6 @@ DISPATCH_GROUP_NUMS=$(node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/node-eval-file.js" "$DISPA
 NODE_EVAL_EOF
 )
 echo '{}' > "$DISPATCH_LINKED_PRS"
-echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"
 if [ -n "$DISPATCH_GROUP_NUMS" ]; then
   if ! node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/resolve-linked-prs.js" "$DISPATCH_GROUP_NUMS" \
     > "$DISPATCH_LINKED_PRS" 2>"$DISPATCH_LINKED_PRS_ERR"; then
diff --git a/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js b/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
--- a/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
+++ b/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
@@ -104,3 +104,20 @@ test('AC5: an unknown reason round-trips through readExclusions but is only matc
   assert.equal(groupIsExcluded([{ number: 42 }], entries, ['oversized', 'firing']), false);
   assert.equal(groupIsExcluded([{ number: 42 }], entries, ['future-reason']), true);
 });
+
+// #1752 left one write to a retired per-reason file behind in queue-pull-script.md's open-PR pass
+// (`echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"`) after its declaration left the session-tmp files map,
+// so bash redirected to an empty path and printed `: No such file or directory` on every pull.
+// Every $DISPATCH_* the script references must be declared in that map or assigned in the script.
+test('queue-pull-script.md: every referenced $DISPATCH_* variable is declared or assigned', () => {
+  const script = fs.readFileSync(
+    path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'plugin', 'skills', 'dispatch', 'queue-pull-script.md'), 'utf8',
+  );
+  const referenced = new Set([...script.matchAll(/\$\{?(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+)/g)].map((m) => m[1]));
+  const declared = new Set([
+    ...[...script.matchAll(/^\s*(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+):\s*'/gm)].map((m) => m[1]),
+    ...[...script.matchAll(/\b(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+)=/g)].map((m) => m[1]),
+  ]);
+  const undeclared = [...referenced].filter((v) => !declared.has(v));
+  assert.deepStrictEqual(undeclared, [], `undeclared variables: ${undeclared.join(', ')}`);
+});
```

**Test:** extend `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` (in the diff): asserts every `$DISPATCH_*` the script references is declared in its `files` map or assigned in the script. Fails on current `main` naming `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED`; passes after the deletion, and guards future migration leftovers.

**Related:** #1752 (closed; the migration that left this line behind).

Surface: infra

## Current State

This record was filed as a `materialize.js` bug: invoked from inside a record's worktree with `--run-dir` pointing at the anchored main-checkout run directory, the materialized spec landed at the worktree-local path `{worktree}/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/work/{n}-spec.md`.

That write is designed behavior, not a resolution bug. `plugin/bin/materialize.js` lines ~290–317 (#1210) deliberately rewrite a `--run-dir` that resolves to the main checkout (or another worktree) into the cwd worktree's equivalent path when cwd is inside a linked worktree, and print a stderr notice saying so. The reason is `materialize.md`'s worktree-first ordering: the spec must land on the feature branch. `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md:67` documents `work/{n}-spec.md` as an exception that "stays inside the worktree".

The real defect is documentation drift: `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` still describes `--run-dir` as "the literal write-location prefix, not a run identity — the CLI writes `{--run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md`" (line 5) and repeats "`--run-dir` is the literal write-location prefix" (line 7). Read literally, both say the main-checkout path is honored from a worktree, which is what led the reflect pass to file this as a bug.

## Deliverables

1. Correct `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` lines 5 and 7 to state that `--run-dir` is the write-location prefix except when cwd is inside a linked worktree and the path resolves elsewhere, in which case the CLI writes to the cwd worktree's equivalent path (#1210), citing `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s `work/{n}-spec.md` exception rather than restating it.
2. Make `materialize.js`'s usage text (and any other plugin prose describing `--run-dir` as literal) agree.
3. If an existing test already covers the #1210 rewrite, reference it in the PR; if none does, add one invoking `materialize.js` from a worktree cwd with a main-checkout `--run-dir` and asserting the worktree-local write plus the stderr notice.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No plugin prose describes `--run-dir` as an unconditional literal write location.
2. `materialize.md` states the worktree-local rewrite and cites `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s exception.
3. A test pins the rewrite behavior, existing or new.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

N/A — documentation correction; no behavior change.

## Technical Approach

Prose edit in `materialize.md`, a check of `materialize.js`'s `USAGE` string, and a repo-wide grep for "literal write-location" and similar phrasing in `plugin/`. No code change to the rewrite itself.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — lines 5 and 7 corrected
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — `USAGE` text, if it says "literal"
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` — cited, not edited

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" `materialize.js` to honor the main-checkout path literally: that would reintroduce the stray main-checkout write #1210 closed.
- Prose conformance tests pin `materialize.md` text; run the full suite.

## Original request

materialize.js writes the spec header to a worktree-relative shadow path instead of the anchored main-checkout run dir

## Current State

During record #2466's build attempt (dispatch drain, 2026-09-18), `materialize.js` was invoked from inside the record's dedicated worktree with `--run-dir` pointed at the anchored main-checkout run directory (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-18T063050-record-2466`, per `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s Anchoring section).
