- Investigate `materialize.js`'s `--run-dir` handling to find where a value that should already be an absolute, anchored path gets re-resolved (or silently re-joined) against the current working directory instead of used as given.
- Fix it so `materialize.js` always writes to the literal `--run-dir` path passed to it, regardless of the caller's cwd (worktree or main checkout).
- Add a regression test: invoke `materialize.js` with an absolute `--run-dir` from a cwd that is NOT that run dir's own ancestor (e.g., a sibling worktree), and assert the spec lands at the given absolute path, not a cwd-relative shadow of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `materialize.js`, invoked from any worktree with an absolute `--run-dir` pointing at the main checkout, writes the materialized header to that literal path -- no worktree-relative shadow copy is created.
- A new regression test reproduces this scenario and fails on the pre-fix code, passes after the fix.
- `npm test` passes in full.

Surface: infra

## Current State

The original request says claude-tweaks "already ships a blast-radius mod that intercepts risky commands (rm -rf, git reset --hard, etc.) and asks Proceed/Cancel". The checkout does not support that premise:

- The only blast-radius code is `plugin/bin/blast-radius.js` (with `plugin/bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js`). It is the gather step of `assess-agent-autonomy`'s merge-check: merge-base resolution, diff numstat, and sensitive-path classification at merge time. It never intercepts a command.
- claude-tweaks ships no mods. Its tool-call interception is the PreToolUse hook (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`), and it only ever emits `permissionDecision: 'deny'` (pre-tool-use.js:422). It never emits an ask prompt, so no claude-tweaks gate can leave an unattended run waiting on a Proceed/Cancel.
- None of its gates targets `rm -rf` or `git reset --hard` (no match for either in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/`).
- Recursive deletion inside claude-tweaks' own unattended machinery runs through Node `fs.rmSync`, not a Bash `rm` command. Examples: `plugin/bin/lib/file-lock.js:115`, `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js:834`, `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js:132`. Shipped skill prose uses only single-file `rm -f` (for example `plugin/skills/_shared/headless-self-report.md:51`).

The external change: Claude Code 2.1.281+ times out a flagged dangerous `rm` prompt after two minutes in unattended, auto, or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` runs, denying the command with a rewrite hint instead of hanging (source in the original request below).

## Deliverables

1. A written comparison, posted as a comment on this record, of the native dangerous-`rm` timeout against what claude-tweaks actually ships. It should cover:
   - the premise correction above: no blast-radius command interceptor exists, and `blast-radius.js` is a merge-time gather;
   - whether any claude-tweaks PreToolUse gate overlaps or conflicts with the native prompt and timeout (expected answer: no, because the gates are deny-only and none targets `rm`);
   - whether any claude-tweaks unattended path (`/claude-tweaks:dispatch`, `/claude-tweaks:flow` auto, Routine firings, `reconcile`) issues a Bash command the native flag would trip, which would now be denied after two minutes rather than hanging;
   - where the "blast-radius mod" in the original request lives, if it exists outside this repo, so the comparison can be redirected there.
2. For any claude-tweaks path the comparison finds the native flag would trip, file a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body. Otherwise, state explicitly that no adjustment is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The comparison comment exists on this record and addresses each of the four points in Deliverable 1, citing the files above.
- It states a clear verdict: no claude-tweaks adjustment needed, or the specific path(s) that need one, each with a linked filed record.
- No claude-tweaks code changes land in this record.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of claude-tweaks' guardrails against Claude Code's native dangerous-rm timeout.

## Technical Approach

A desk comparison. Confirm the deny-only posture of `pre-tool-use.js` and the absence of Bash recursive-`rm` in shipped skill prose and `bin/` code with a repo-wide grep. Then read the native permission-modes documentation for the exact trigger set, which may cover more than `rm`, and re-check the unattended paths against that set.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/blast-radius.js` — the only blast-radius code; merge-time gather, not an interceptor
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — the PreToolUse gates; deny-only
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — representative unattended recursive deletion via `fs.rmSync`

## Gotchas

- The original request's premise of a shipped blast-radius mod is contradicted by the checkout. #3055 lists a "blast-radius-style guardrail" only as a candidate for a future mod. Do not build one under this record; that is #3055's evaluation.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the native flag fires only on Bash-tool commands, not on Node `fs.rmSync` inside a hook or CLI subprocess. Confirm from the permission-modes documentation.
- The native trigger set may widen across Claude Code versions. Cite the version the comparison was made against.

## Original request

Compare blast-radius against Claude Code's native dangerous-rm timeout

Current State:
- Claude Code (2.1.281+) now times out a flagged dangerous rm prompt after two minutes in unattended/auto/--dangerously-skip-permissions runs, denying the command with a rewrite hint instead of hanging.
- claude-tweaks already ships a blast-radius mod that intercepts risky commands (rm -rf, git reset --hard, etc.) and asks Proceed/Cancel.

Deliverables:
- Check whether blast-radius's own unattended-run behavior overlaps or conflicts with this native timeout.
- Align blast-radius's timeout/denial behavior with the native one where it makes sense, or document why it intentionally differs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A written comparison of the two behaviors.
- Any needed blast-radius adjustment made or explicitly deferred with a reason.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#critical-paths

Surface: infra

## Current State

The audit the original request asks for has a known answer at shaping time: a repo-wide `git grep -i -E 'thinking_?disabled|between_tools'` returns zero hits. Nothing in `plugin/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `evals/`, or the project's `.claude/` references either spelling.

claude-tweaks does not set a thinking mode anywhere. It controls models through two settings:

- Agent and routine frontmatter set `model:` and `effort:` only. `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` uses `model: sonnet` and `effort: medium`. Every `plugin/skills/*/routine-template.yml` carries a `model:` line, for example `plugin/skills/specify/routine-template.yml:7` `model: claude-sonnet-5`.
- Subagent dispatches resolve a model profile through `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js`. The profiles (`plugin/bin/lib/model-profiles/profiles.js:15-18`) carry `model` and `effort` fields only, and effort reaches the agent as a prompt line, not an API thinking setting (`profiles.js:27-29`).

The external change: Claude Sonnet 5.5 renames the no-upfront-thinking setting from `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools` (source in the original request below).

`docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is where this repo records per-model deltas that affect how skills are authored. It currently has a Fable 5.1 entry (line 233) and no Sonnet 5.5 entry.

## Deliverables

1. Re-run the zero-usage audit at build time (the grep above, repo-wide, both spellings) and record the result in this record's closing comment.
2. Add one short Sonnet 5.5 bullet to the "Model-version prompting notes" section of `docs/skill-authoring.md`. It should state the `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools` rename, cite the migration guide, and say that claude-tweaks sets no thinking mode today (model and effort only), so nothing needs migrating. Any future agent, routine template, or profile that adds a thinking setting should use `between_tools` when targeting Sonnet 5.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The build-time grep for `thinkingdisabled` (case-insensitive, with and without an underscore) returns zero hits outside the new note.
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Model-version prompting notes section carries a Sonnet 5.5 bullet naming both spellings and linking the migration guide.
- CLAUDE.md is unchanged. The note belongs in the model-version section, not the always-loaded file, which has a line budget.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This records the Sonnet 5.5 thinking-setting rename in claude-tweaks' authoring notes; no configuration needed migrating.

## Technical Approach

A documentation-only change. Re-run the grep, then add the bullet next to the existing Fable 5.1 entry, following its source-cited format. If the build-time grep unexpectedly finds a usage, migrate it in the same change, scoped to settings that target `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and list it in the closing comment.

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — Model-version prompting notes section gains the Sonnet 5.5 bullet
- `plugin/bin/lib/model-profiles/profiles.js` — profile fields (model, effort) confirmed to carry no thinking setting
- `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` — the one shipped agent's model and effort frontmatter

## Gotchas

- The original request assumed claude-tweaks "may still reference the old flag". The shaping-time grep contradicts that, so no migration is expected. Do not invent a thinking setting just to have something to rename.
- Routine templates pin `claude-sonnet-5`, not `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Bumping their model is a separate decision, out of scope here.

## Original request

Audit claude-tweaks configs for the thinkingdisabled rename

Current State:
- Claude Sonnet 5.5 renames the no-upfront-thinking setting from `thinkingdisabled` to `between_tools`.
- claude-tweaks defines multiple subagents/skills with model and thinking settings that may still reference the old flag.

Deliverables:
- Audit claude-tweaks' agent/skill definitions for any `thinkingdisabled` usage.
- Migrate any found usages to `between_tools` when targeting claude-sonnet-5-5.

Acceptance Criteria:
- No remaining `thinkingdisabled` references that target Sonnet 5.5.
- A short note in CLAUDE.md or the relevant skill doc about the rename.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `registerCheck('carrier-commit', ...)` has a ground-truth fallback for issues with no textual carrier commit (`missingTextual`). It first calls `fetchLinkedPRs` once for every number in `missingTextual` (`engine-verify.js:392-394`). That is one batched, aliased GraphQL call built by `buildLinkedPRQuery` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js:729-735`). The loop that follows (`engine-verify.js:398-405`) then runs one `deps.gh(['issue', 'view', String(n), '--json', 'state'], cwd)` per issue that has a closing-PR reference, only to learn whether that issue is `CLOSED`.

The same per-issue alias in `buildLinkedPRQuery` already selects `number`, `closedByPullRequestsReferences` and `timelineItems`. Selecting `state` there too would let the fallback read the issue state from the batched result and drop the per-issue subprocess. `fetchLinkedPRs` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js:40-83`) builds each Map value as `{ openPR, mentions, hasClosingPRReference }` (`:81`), so the new field has to be passed through there as well.

The impact is small: zero to a few issues per wrap-up verify. This is a cleanup, not a defect. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3d, reproduced by both agents, refutation not-refuted; ledger row 2).

## Deliverables

1. `buildLinkedPRQuery`'s per-issue alias also selects the issue's own `state`. The field is additive, so existing consumers that ignore it are unaffected.
2. `fetchLinkedPRs` passes that value through on each Map entry, for example as `issueState`. The name must not collide with the existing PR-level `state` inside `mentions`.
3. The carrier-commit fallback in `engine-verify.js` reads the issue state from the batched `fetchLinkedPRs` result instead of calling `gh issue view` once per issue. When the batched field is missing, the issue is treated as still missing, which matches today's degrade-to-`stillMissing` posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With N issues in `missingTextual`, all of them carrying a closing-PR reference, the carrier-commit check makes exactly one `gh` call. A test in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` counts the injected `deps.gh` invocations and asserts this. Prove it goes red by restoring the per-issue `gh issue view` loop.
- A fallback issue whose batched state is `CLOSED` with a closing-PR reference passes, and one whose state is `OPEN` stays in `stillMissing`, matching current behavior.
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/linked-prs.test.js` asserts the new pass-through field.
- `tests/resolve-linked-prs-cli.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/issues/record.test.js` and the dispatch eligibility tests pass unchanged.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Wrap-up's carrier-commit check now reads issue state from its existing batched query, with no extra GitHub call per issue.

## Technical Approach

Add `state` next to `number` in the alias string inside `buildLinkedPRQuery`. In `fetchLinkedPRs`, read `node.state` and set it on the result entry under a distinct name (`issueState`). In `engine-verify.js`, replace the `deps.gh(['issue', 'view', ...])` try/catch with `entry.issueState`. The existing `stillMissing` logic stays as it is.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` — `buildLinkedPRQuery`: select the issue's `state` in each alias
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js` — `fetchLinkedPRs`: pass the issue state through on each Map entry
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — carrier-commit fallback: read the batched state and remove the per-issue `gh issue view`
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — runner-call-count test for the fallback
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/linked-prs.test.js` — pass-through field assertion

## Gotchas

- Fake GraphQL responses in existing tests (`linked-prs.test.js`, `resolve-linked-prs-cli.test.js`, `engine-verify.test.js`) will not carry `state` on the issue node. The engine-verify fallback must treat a missing `issueState` as not-closed, so those fixtures still pass and a malformed response never reads as `CLOSED`.
- `mentions[].state` is a PR's state, while the new field is the issue's state. Keep the names distinct so `shipped-candidate.js`'s `classifyShipped` never confuses them.
- `buildLinkedPRQuery` is also used by `/dispatch`'s open-linked-PR exclusion (`partitionByOpenLinkedPR`). An extra scalar field in the alias is harmless there, but check that no test pins the exact query string. At shaping time `git grep` found none outside `record.js` itself.

## Original request

wrap-up engine-verify: carrier-commit fallback runs one gh issue view per issue instead of reading state from the batched query

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s carrier-commit ground-truth fallback (lines ~397-404) runs one `gh issue view N --json state` subprocess per issue in `missingTextual`, immediately after `fetchLinkedPRs` (line ~391) already made one batched, aliased GraphQL call for the same issue numbers via `buildLinkedPRQuery` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js:729-735`). Adding `state` to that per-issue alias would remove the loop. Impact is small (zero to a few issues per wrap-up verify), so this is a cleanup, not a defect. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3d, reproduced by both agents, refutation not-refuted; ledger row 2).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `buildLinkedPRQuery`'s per-issue alias also selects the issue's `state`, passed through by `fetchLinkedPRs` (additive field — other consumers unaffected)
- [ ] The carrier-commit fallback reads `state` from that batched result instead of one `gh issue view` per issue

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The carrier-commit check issues exactly one `gh` call for N missing issues (pinned by a test counting runner calls)
- [ ] `resolve-linked-prs.js`, `shipped-candidate.js` and dispatch eligibility tests pass unchanged
